rubric.why: Identifies qualitative data by its categorical or descriptive nature.
rubric.description: Names qualitative data and identifies it as categories or labels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer includes “qualitative” and either “categories” or “labels”. The idea that it describes qualities rather than quantity may also be expressed in different words.

rubric.why: Identifies quantitative data as numerical and concerned with amount.
rubric.description: Names quantitative data and explains that numbers are used to measure quantity or amount.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer includes “quantitative”, “numbers”, and either “measure” or “quantity”.

modelAnswer: Qualitative data refer to categories or labels used to describe the qualities or characteristics of something rather than its quantity. Quantitative data consists of numbers used to measure the quantity or amount of something.

rubric.why: Correctly classifies the number of students as discrete data.
Explains that discrete values are countable and separate, commonly whole numbers.
rubric.description: States that discrete data consists of countable, separate or distinct values, often whole numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the values as countable and separate/distinct, or as countable whole numbers.

modelAnswer: It is discrete data because discrete data consist of distinct, separate values that are countable, often in whole numbers.

rubric.why: Recognises a benefit of organising data before analysis.
rubric.description: States that organising data can reduce errors, save time or improve clarity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying at least one of these benefits.

rubric.why: Explains that visual formats make data easier to interpret and use.
rubric.description: States that tables, charts or graphs make data easier to understand, compare or analyse, helping with conclusions or decisions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking a table, chart or graph with understanding, comparison, analysis, conclusions or decisions.

modelAnswer: Organising data helps reduce errors, saves time and improves clarity. Tables, charts and graphs make data easier to understand, compare and analyse, so it is simpler to draw conclusions and make decisions.

rubric.why: States the main benefit of visualization: making data easier to understand.
rubric.description: Explains that data visualization makes understanding data easier.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when the answer links visualization/visualisation with understanding data.

rubric.why: Identifies insights visualization can reveal or provide.
rubric.description: States that charts or graphs reveal patterns, trends or relationships, or provide quick insights.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying at least two of these insights or for linking charts/graphs with quick insights.

modelAnswer: Data visualization makes understanding data much easier. Charts and graphs help us quickly see patterns, trends and relationships, and provide quick insights without having to read through all the details.

rubric.why: Identifies the purpose of a line graph as showing change over time.
rubric.description: States that a line graph shows how data changes over time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking a line graph with data changes or trends over time.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of data displayed over time.
rubric.description: Gives monthly sales figures or temperature readings over several days as an example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant time-based example such as monthly sales or temperature readings over days.

modelAnswer: A line graph can show how data changes over time. For example, it could show monthly sales figures or temperature readings over several days.

rubric.why: Defines data collection as a process of gathering information or data.
rubric.description: States that data collection is the process of gathering information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining data collection as a process involving gathering or collecting information/data.

rubric.why: States a purpose of collecting data.
rubric.description: Explains that data is gathered to answer questions, make decisions or understand something better.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one stated purpose.

modelAnswer: Data collection is the process of gathering information to answer questions, make decisions, or understand something better.
